Coram:

Justice M.S. Sahoo
 Order
19.10.2023 Order No. Hybrid Mode 04. 1.

The BLAPL has been filed under Section 439 Cr.P.C. seeking release on bail, by the petitioner,
who is in jail custody in connection with B. Bazar P.S. Case No.224 dated 04.06.2023 corresponding to G.R. Case No.1300 of 2022 pending in the court of learned S.D.J.M., Berhampur, for alleged commission of offence under Sections 420/406/467/468/471/34 of IPC.

2. When the matter was taken up on 16.10.2023, the following order was passed:
"1.
The allegations against the petitioner is that he has mortgaged the property without knowledge of the owner before two banks and swindled the money.
The owner of the property faces auction of his property by the bank though concededly the bank has not advanced any loan to the actual owner of the property.
2. Learned Senior Counsel appearing for the petitioner submits that this Court is not sitting to // 2 // recover the amount defalcated/cheated by the petitioner.

It is submitted by the learned Senior Counsel that unless he is released, he is unable to arrange the money that he has been advised to repay the remaining amount of loan account to the Bank to show him indulgence as far as prayer for bail is concerned.
3. Learned Additional Standing Counsel for the State submits that the self-same house has been mortgaged twice by the present accused.
4. Miss Patra, learned counsel for the informant submits that the two loans are yet to be repaid by the informant.

Learned Senior Counsel in response though does not dispute that two loans have been taken from two different banks without involvement/ knowledge of the actual owner of the property but submits on instruction that one of the loan account has already been liquidated as the amount has been repayed by the petitioner and in the present account as per the statement furnished by the bank Rs.6,94,000/- is still to be paid which the petitioner has been advised to deposit to liquidate the loan account.

5. In considered opinion of this Court, this Court has not passed any order as far as recovery of the amount is concerned, the petitioner on his own being advised to repay the loan, has done the same, perhaps with an intention to seek indulgence of the Court while seeking bail as concededly the loans have been given by the Bank without the knowledge/involvement of the owner of the property and the money has been allegedly received by the petitioner.
Learned Senior Counsel seeks adjournment to obtain up-to-date instruction.

6. As prayed for, list on 19.10.2023."
3.

It is submitted by the learned Senior Counsel appearing for the petitioner that the petitioner given a chance, if is granted bail, he shall clear the dues to the bank within six weeks from the date of release.

// 3 // It is further submitted that the petitioner shall abide by all the terms and conditions that would be imposed for grant of bail, he being a local person having roots in the society shall subject himself to the jurisdiction of the court in seisin of the matter.
4. Learned Additional Standing Counsel for the State referring to the materials contained in the case diary opposes the prayer for bail of the petitioner.

5. The learned counsel for the informant again reiterates her submission that behind the back of the informant, his property has been mortgaged by the petitioner to secure a loan out of which about of Rupees seven lakhs remain outstanding and the informant has been put to unnecessary harassment by the activity of the petitioner as the lender Bank has initiated securitisation process for recovery of Babula Nayak vs State Of Odisha ....

sentences.text:

2 the entire loan due.

In response, the learned Senior Counsel appearing for the petitioner reiterates his submission that the petitioner will clear the dues of the bank within six weeks from the date he is released on bail, if granted.

6. Having heard the learned Senior Counsel appearing for the petitioner, the learned Additional Standing Counsel for the State and the learned counsel for the informant, this Court is inclined to grant bail to the petitioner subject to such stringent terms and conditions that would be imposed by the learned court in seisin of the matter, which shall also include a condition as has been stated on behalf of the petitioner at the bar today that the petitioner has been advised to // 4 // clear the due of the bank within six weeks from the date of his release on bail.

It is also directed that there shall be a further condition that any violation of/deviation from any of the terms and conditions that would be imposed for grant bail of bail, shall result in filing of the petition for cancellation of bail by the informant/victim/law enforcement agency.
7. The BLAPL is disposed of, accordingly.
Issue urgent certified copy as per rules.
(M.S. Sahoo)
